name: file-watcher
title: File watcher — part 2 of native-memory: watch a path and mirror the filesystem into memory

cards.card: Missed events while the server is down
cards.ruling: Each watch keeps a last-change timestamp; on restart, targets changed since it are re-ingested (catch-up). No stale state — goes straight to processing.
Overwrite — the incoming content wins; the target's previous chunks are replaced.
OS-agnostic: Path.GetFullPath (absolute, separators and '..' resolved, trailing separator stripped); case comparison follows the host OS filesystem.

cards.card: Unit-level scenarios (concurrency, watcher-loop containment, hash-skip internals)

cards.ruling: Project-scoped only; no global/workspace-scoped watches; all three tools take projectId.
memory_watch_add/remove require rw+; memory_watch_status open to every tier; background mirroring runs regardless of tier (tiers gate direct agent operations only).

cards.card: Are watches 'settings that affect other agents'?
cards.ruling: No — rw may add/remove watches; the ro tier may not.
Opt-in: watching disabled until explicitly enabled; watch paths must be inside a scope allowlist entry (absolute path covers the directory and all subdirectories; no '*' needed).

CLI-only, user-facing (no MCP tools, no env/args, no config-file edits; no access-tier checks). Format: watch enable|disable {project-id|*} {true|false}, watch scope add|remove|list {project-id|*} {path}, watch concurrency {project-id|*} {1..16} (default 4); '*' matches all projects, more specific entry wins. Single-channel principle (f:): added CLI options remove other config channels.

in: Three MCP tools: memory_watch_add / memory_watch_status / memory_watch_remove, all project-scoped (projectId), identified per (projectId, path)
Watches are project-scoped only; no global or workspace-scoped watches
Watching is opt-in: disabled until explicitly enabled; watch paths must be inside a scope allowlist entry (absolute path, covers directory + all subdirectories)

Watch configuration is CLI-only and user-facing: watch enable|disable {project-id|*} {true|false}, watch scope add|remove|list {project-id|*} {path}, watch concurrency {project-id|*} {1..16} (default 4); '*' matches all projects, more specific entry wins; no access-tier checks; persisted across restarts
Watches accept both single files and directories; a directory watch covers its subtree
Initial scan is asynchronous: add returns immediately, status reports scanning until the seed digest completes
All four filesystem event types (created/changed/renamed/deleted) enter the pipeline
Mirror semantics 1:1: delete removes the file's chunks from memory; rename removes old-path chunks and re-digests under the new path (overwrite on collision)
SmartRAG-inspired mechanics: debounce (1s tick), hash-skip (path+content SHA-256), initial scan, retry (exponential backoff; after 5 failures stop checking but keep registration/status)
Pipeline: single channel of events -> per-path pending aggregation -> 1s tick -> per-path digests with configured concurrency limit (default 4), round-robin across watches
Missed-event catch-up: per-watch last-change timestamp; on restart, targets changed since it are re-ingested
Containment: watch failures never fail the MCP server; errors surface through memory_watch_status
Idempotency: add on an already-watched (projectId, path) is a no-op; remove on a non-existent watch is a no-op
Access tiers: add/remove require rw+; status open to every tier; background mirroring runs regardless of tier
Status states: scanning / healthy / retrying / stopped; status returns watch states, last error, last sync
out: MCP-tool-based watch configuration (enable/scope are CLI-only, not agent tools)
Wildcard path scopes ('*' at the end of a path)
Stale status state (removed; catch-up replaces it)
env/args config channels for watch settings (--watch-enable / --watch-scope) — converted by the CLI-config task (f: single channel)
memory_inspect introspection tool and metrics/tracing (part-2 siblings, already deferred in part-1)
Full CLI config surface for all server options — separate task (design subagent 2026-08-04, docs/work/archive/2026-08-04-cli-config-findings.md)

nonFunctional: Watch operation failures are contained: no watch failure ever fails the MCP server or its other tools
Concurrency: per-path digests, global limit default 4, round-robin across watches (fairness, no starvation)
Retry: exponential backoff, max 5 attempts, then stop checking but keep status
Persistence: watches table and watch configuration survive restarts (restart re-watches; catch-up ingests missed changes)
TDD mandatory: scenario tests pin mirror/delete/rename semantics; unit-level scenarios (concurrency, loop containment, hash-skip) kept as implementation tests
TreatWarningsAsErrors; dotnet build + dotnet test green
No hardcoded secrets; watch configuration via CLI only

targets.implementation: src/AiRaccoon.Infrastructure (watches table, watcher pipeline) + src/AiRaccoon.Core (domain) + src/AiRaccoon (CLI commands, MCP tools)

risks: Delete/rename propagation is destructive and irreversible — mirror removal is the highest-risk merge surface; dedicated scenario tests required
Filesystem event loss/coalescing differs per OS (FileSystemWatcher semantics) — catch-up timestamp is the safety net; verify on linux/macOS/windows
Initial scan of a large directory is unbounded work — async by contract; status must report scanning and errors
Hash-skip correctness: a real content change must never be skipped (path+content SHA-256 per D8 identity)
Concurrency limit + round-robin fairness need unit-level verification (not black-box observable)
